findings.text: the refusal tests len(completed.stdout.split()) != 1, but sacct prints a multi-node allocation as one compressed hostlist token: sacct -j 1207375 -X -n -o NodeList prints 98dci4-clu-[50+ (the 14-node allocation 98dci4-clu-[5073-5086] at default column width) and receipts_host returns that string as though it were a hostname, where the goal required refusal rather than a guess; reproduced on the head tree, latent only because no receipts file in the production directory today carries a multi-node job and the helper has no production caller.

the multi-node case is modelled as sacct printing node-a and node-b on two lines, a shape this cluster's sacct does not produce, so the test asserts a refusal for a fixture that cannot occur and covers nothing about the one multi-node form that does -- the single compressed token that imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:370 returns as a host.

the anchor states that the helper raises when sacct prints anything other than exactly one node and that a host is never inferred, which a multi-node allocation's one-token output contradicts, so the landed record claims a refusal the code does not implement.

the gate, ruff and negative-control logs all stamp rev=d9e89c5b while their trees and content measure the repaired working tree -- the commit that content became, a08c59a8, is dated 09:08:46, after all three logs were written at 09:06 -- so the same revision label appears on the 34-passed base measurement and the 38-passed repaired one and a reader keying by revision cannot tell which content a number came from; the manifest itself names a08c59a8 correctly, so the defect is in the log headers.
